subject: Performance follow-up: p95/p99 latency targets & hosted vs current provider

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance follow-up: p95/p99 latency targets & next steps

Hi Ellen —

Great call this morning, thanks for walking through ShopGrid's realtime summarization use case. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a representative hosted evaluation: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- End-to-end inference SLOs: target p95/p99 for a single-shot completion (full response delivered)
- Streaming requirement: token-level streaming to clients (SSE) to render partial results as they arrive
- Typical request profile: avg prompt ~120 tokens, avg completion ~300 tokens; 99th percentile completion up to 1,200 tokens
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrent sessions ~150; burst concurrency up to ~200–250
- Throughput: steady QPS ~20 req/s; burst up to ~80 req/s for short windows

From our quick notes you mentioned current provider numbers (ballpark): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~980ms end-to-end for the same flows. Correct?

As next steps, can you please share: 
1) a small sample set of payloads (anonymized) representative of the 50/80/99 token-length buckets (you can use sample-payloads.jsonl)
2) current latency export (CSV) for the last 30 days — p50/p95/p99 and any per-region splits (we'll accept what you already exported)
3) preferred test window (date/time) to run a short load test from our hosted environment against a staging endpoint

What we'll do after we get those:
- Redwood will run two targeted hosted tests: (A) streaming mode with progressive token flush, (B) non-streaming end-to-end.
- We'll report observed end-to-end p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU token-s/sec, and tail behavior under concurrency.
- If hosted numbers look good we'll propose a canary plan and a 30-day evaluation quota.

Attachments: I included a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) as a placeholder for timing + milestones.

Thanks — if you want us to change any of the test parameters before we spin up tests let me know.

Ben Carter

Ben — thanks for the recap and for the MAP. Confirming a few items and attaching the export you asked for.

Quick clarifications:
- Current provider: we run a managed endpoint from CurrentAI (multi-tenant hosted).
- Observed averages (last 30 days, us-west customers): p50 ~180ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~980ms. Spikes happen during concurrency surges and when long responses (>=1,000 tokens) are common.
- Streaming: yes, SSE; our UI expects early tokens within ~200ms of start, then steady streaming thereafter. If initial latency is >300ms users complain.
- For tokens: the distribution is heavily long-tailed; median completion ~300 tokens but ~4% of requests are >1,000 tokens.

Attachments included: shopgrid-current-latency-report.csv, sample-payloads.jsonl (anonymized).

We can do a test window this Friday 2026-03-20 between 09:00–12:00 PT. We'll open a staging DNS entry and can whitelist your test IPs.

Thanks — quick technical read on the artifacts ShopGrid provided and proposed test config: 

Findings from CSV + payloads:
- Long tail confirmed: ~3–5% requests >1k tokens; that drives p99 on CurrentAI due to batching pressure and network jitter.
- Current p95/p99 gap indicates caching and batching parameters aren't tuned for their workload.

Proposed hosted test configuration (us-west region):
- Runtime: Redwood hosted API (dedicated single-tenant pool for the trial)
- Model variant: rdx-4k-quant (optimized kernel path for streaming)
- Pool size: 4 GPU workers, each with 2 inference shards — target aggregate concurrency headroom ~240 concurrent streams
- Batching: dynamic continuous batching with 30ms coalescing window and separate queue for streaming flows to avoid tail amplification
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for repeated system prompts; set TTL 5m for trial
- Network: fronted by regional edge in us-west to reduce e2e RTT

Suggested test parameters:
- Steady-state: 20 QPS with concurrency 150 for 15 minutes
- Burst test: ramp to 80 QPS over 60s, hold 5 minutes, then ramp down
- Long tail extraction: inject 5–10% of requests >1k tokens to measure p99 impact
- Streaming behavior: verify \"first token\" latency target <=200ms and maintain streaming throughput >= 30 tokens/sec per stream for longer responses

Success criteria (for the hosted run):
- End-to-end p95 <=250ms, p99 <=700ms for the mixed request mix
- First-token in streaming path <=200ms for 95% of stream starts
- No more than 2% request error rate under burst conditions

Operational asks from ShopGrid for Friday test:
- Whitelist test source IPs (we'll send these tomorrow)
- A staging DNS entry + ephemeral API key for the test
- Confirmation of the exact time window (we confirm 09:00–12:00 PT)

I'll provision a short trial dedicated pool and share endpoints and credentials in a secure link (redwood internal CI page). If the Friday window works we can have test endpoints ready by Thursday EOD.

-Vivek
